scope: A plain-English name for every opcode docs/g17-tensorops-machine-model.md cites; rendered as its section 0.16 by tools/g17opglossary.py
warning: Names are this project's, chosen by measured function; they are not Apple's spellings. `mnemonic` is agxforge.g17.slice's key (EXECUTED_NAMES where it corrects KNOWN_OPS) and is never renamed.

opcodes.name: uniform register file, decoder tag
opcodes.what: Not an instruction: Apple's decoder writes the uniform register file as op0 inside operands such as bin(op0,const(K),4).

opcodes.name: message staging file, decoder tag
opcodes.what: Not an instruction: Apple's decoder writes the message staging register file as op4; a message instruction waits on the scoreboard slot of a write into it.

opcodes.name: 32-bit AND with immediate
opcodes.what: d = a32 & imm; the register-immediate member of the and-width matrix.

opcodes.name: 32-bit AND
opcodes.what: d = a32 & b32, two 32-bit registers.

opcodes.name: 16-bit AND with immediate, 32-bit result
opcodes.what: d32 = a16 & imm; used for masks such as t & (S-1) and SR_TG_X & 255.

opcodes.name: 16-bit AND, 32-bit result
opcodes.what: d32 = a16 & b16 with the mask taken from a constant-pool operand (a register mask returned zero for every lane).

opcodes.name: 16-bit AND with immediate
opcodes.what: d16 = a16 & imm; emitted by `a & 0xf` on ushort, used to mask nibbles in the fp4 unpack (not a shift). Executed on Apple's GPU over 4,096 lanes at immediates 15, 63, 255 (25.192).

opcodes.name: 16-bit AND
opcodes.what: d16 = a16 & b16, emitted by `a & b` on ushort.

opcodes.name: 32-bit AND with immediate into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` AND: a32 & imm written to the uniform/staging file rather than a register.

opcodes.name: threadgroup barrier
opcodes.what: threadgroup_barrier with a memory-scope operand (also the imageblock barrier); NOT a device fence: another core's stores stay invisible.

opcodes.name: call
opcodes.what: Apple's subroutine call; Apple's own program using it runs 32/32 in our image path, cc still inlines calls.

opcodes.name: conditional back-edge branch
opcodes.what: the loop back edge; taken per the exec mask that op582 establishes (op579 does not gate it).

opcodes.name: skip branch, no active lanes
opcodes.what: forward branch placed after a region's op582, taken when no lane of the simdgroup is active, landing on the region's exec restore.

opcodes.name: population count
opcodes.what: d = number of set bits in a32.

opcodes.name: move immediate, two-operand form
opcodes.what: writes an immediate into a register; Apple's matmul uses it to zero the accumulators.

opcodes.name: 16-bit move immediate into a half
opcodes.what: dst16 = imm (byte 2 of the 4-byte form); main writes 0 to clear a half before the register is read as a 32-bit index. Modelled for immediate 0; a nonzero immediate is written as unknown bits (25.184).

opcodes.name: exec pop, restore mask
opcodes.what: pops the exec-mask stack, restoring the mask from before the enclosing if/loop region.

opcodes.name: while-exec, set mask in place
opcodes.what: sets the exec mask absolutely from a predicate and overwrites the top stack entry; Apple's loop latch uses it but it does not gate op458.

opcodes.name: return
opcodes.what: Apple's subroutine return (terminator).

opcodes.name: exec push, if, from flag
opcodes.what: pushes the exec mask and narrows it by the flag a compare (op10369) wrote; opens a guarded region closed by op577; gates op458.

opcodes.name: 32-bit register move
opcodes.what: copies one 32-bit register to another; also moves a constant-program-published uniform into place.

opcodes.name: 16-bit register move
opcodes.what: copies one 16-bit half register; Apple uses it to clear a low half once.

opcodes.name: uniform / staging write
opcodes.what: in the constant program writes a uniform register (slot field 0); in a main program writes the op4 message staging file with scoreboard slot 1-8 that the consumer waits on.

opcodes.name: publish sibling, function unknown
opcodes.what: the opcode op592 becomes when b0[3] flips; 0 instances in either corpus, function unknown.

opcodes.name: fragment spill store
opcodes.what: stores a register to a stack slot (slot index steps 2 per 32-bit register); the fragment spill, beside op17789 scalar spills.

opcodes.name: range mask, immediate width
opcodes.what: range4: bit j of a 4-bit result is set iff lo <= src + j < lo + w, lo and w 8-bit immediates; feeds a masked load's operand 9.

opcodes.name: range mask, register width
opcodes.what: range4 with the width w read from a 32-bit register instead of an immediate; the window wraps modulo 2^32.

opcodes.name: range mask, 16-bit source
opcodes.what: range4 from a 16-bit source register.

opcodes.name: end of program
opcodes.what: END terminator, one per program.

opcodes.name: half add with float immediate
opcodes.what: half(a + K), rounded once (through fp32 is the same function on every half), subnormals kept, NaN -> the canonical quiet NaN; executed on Apple's GPU (25.195).

opcodes.name: fp16 fma, register form
opcodes.what: binary16 a*b + c rounded once (0 of 196,608 triples off the exact rounding on hardware, subnormals and overflow included); sources are low (425+n) or high (281+n) halves; emitted by cc as fma16 / tensor_acc_fma16 (25.196).

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup MMA, f16
opcodes.what: The pre-tensor-unit simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply-accumulate with half operands and half accumulate; 42 vendor instances, all 14 bytes.

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup multiply, f16
opcodes.what: The legacy simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply without an accumulator, half precision.

opcodes.name: fp32 saturate
opcodes.what: Clamps an fp32 value to [0, 1] (Metal `saturate`); the true fsat, not op1062.

opcodes.name: fp32 add
opcodes.what: d = a + b in fp32; the accumulate step of Apple's reductions.

opcodes.name: fp32 add, rare alternate encoding
opcodes.what: d = a + b in fp32, a distinct byte encoding from op998/op1061 (same measured-family semantics); table-only evidence (68 corpus instances) so the encoding difference from op998 is not decoded. Seen in MLX's compiled affine_qmv_fast dequant loop.

opcodes.name: half to fp32 widening
opcodes.what: Converts a 16-bit half to fp32; the map's `fadd.imm` is wrong (EXECUTED_NAMES cvt.f16.f32).

opcodes.name: fp32 add with float immediate
opcodes.what: d = a + imm with an 8-bit float-coded immediate (D1006.l12: +1.0 on four inputs; the formwidths receipt).

opcodes.name: fp32 add, half result
opcodes.what: d16 = a32 + b32, rounded once to half (nearest even), overflow to inf (D1014, z1014, t1014).

opcodes.name: fp32 plus half, half result
opcodes.what: d16 = a32 + b16, rounded to half.

opcodes.name: fp32 to half narrowing
opcodes.what: Converts fp32 to half; Apple's recipe wraps eight of these around a half-output accumulator.

opcodes.name: fp32 add with immediate into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` fadd.imm: result written to the uniform/staging file; a 6-byte constant-program ALU form.

opcodes.name: fp32 to bfloat16 narrowing, unconfirmed
opcodes.what: Writes a 16-bit value from an fp32 source; the map calls it a half add-immediate, but section 25.13 counts it as the narrowing around the bfloat accumulator and its constructs are all bfloat. Unresolved.

opcodes.name: fp32 add, common alternate encoding
opcodes.what: d = a + b in fp32, a distinct byte encoding from op998/op1001 (same measured-family semantics, 511 corpus instances); the encoding difference from op998 is not decoded. Seen alongside op998 in MLX's compiled affine_qmv_fast dequant loop.

opcodes.name: fine x-derivative, saturated
opcodes.what: Cross-lane `dfdx` (fine) with saturation; not fsat (that is op904).

opcodes.name: hardware exp2
opcodes.what: 2^x in one instruction; within 1 ulp, correctly rounded on 632 of 1,024 probes.

opcodes.name: fp32 fused multiply-add
opcodes.what: d = a * b + c in fp32, all three from registers.

opcodes.name: fp32 FMA, literal addend
opcodes.what: d = a * b + literal; `fma(a, b, 1.0f)` reaches it and computes a*b + 1.0 exactly.

opcodes.name: fp32 FMA, literal multiplicand
opcodes.what: The FMA form a literal operand selects (`mix(a, b, 0.25f)`, `sinpi`); beyond that route its semantics are unmeasured.

opcodes.name: fp32 FMA with two float immediates
opcodes.what: d = a * K1 + K2, both 8-bit float immediates (u2200, 31 cases; the formwidths receipt a*6 + 4); the map's fadd.imm name is the adjacency guess.

opcodes.name: fp32 fused multiply-add, alternate encoding
opcodes.what: d = a * b + c in fp32, a distinct byte encoding from op2190 (same measured-family semantics, 288 corpus instances); the encoding difference from op2190 is not decoded (not the literal-addend or literal-multiplicand forms of op2192/op2198). The FMA that follows the op2240 candidate in MLX's compiled affine_qmv_fast dequant loop.

opcodes.name: FMA-family variant, narrow operand, unconfirmed
opcodes.what: Schedclass 56 like op2190/op2192/op2198, zero corpus instances; appears in MLX's compiled affine_qmv_fast dequant loop. unconfirmed: likely another FMA-family variant with a narrow operand; its operand fields are not decoded.

opcodes.name: fused multiply-add, schedclass-87 base form
opcodes.what: The contract's ffma at schedclass 87 (8 operands, 1 definition), cited as the base form that op2433 narrows; not emitted or measured by this project.

opcodes.name: fp32 FMA into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` ffma: a*b + c written to the uniform/staging file; 8-byte constant-program form.

opcodes.name: fused multiply-add, narrowed form
opcodes.what: A narrowed form of op2241; in MLX's quantized-matmul dequant it computes q*s + b. Seen only in MLX's binary, never emitted by us.

opcodes.name: hardware log2
opcodes.what: log2(x) in one instruction.

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup MMA, fp32
opcodes.what: Legacy simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply-accumulate in fp32; what matmul2d float falls to without relaxed_precision (no tensor-unit MMA emitted).

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup multiply, fp32
opcodes.what: Legacy simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply without accumulator in fp32; emitted beside op2842 by fp32 matmul2d.

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup MMA, f16 in fp32 out
opcodes.what: Legacy simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply-accumulate taking half operands and an fp32 accumulator.

opcodes.name: legacy 8x8 simdgroup MMA, bf16
opcodes.what: Legacy simdgroup_matrix 8x8 multiply-accumulate with bfloat16 operands.

opcodes.name: fp32 multiply
opcodes.what: d = a * b in fp32, both from registers.

opcodes.name: fp32 times half multiply
opcodes.what: d32 = a32 * b16 (mixed-precision multiply).

opcodes.name: fp32 op with float immediate, unconfirmed
opcodes.what: Mapped as `fadd.imm`; section 25.84 pairs it with op3290 the way op2192 pairs with op2190, suggesting a literal-operand multiply. Which one it is has not been separated.

opcodes.name: fp32 multiply, half result
opcodes.what: d16 = a32 * b32, rounded to half (m3306; the width receipt's 0x3e00 rules out bf16).

opcodes.name: fp32 multiply into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` fmul: a*b written to the uniform/staging file (also an op4 staging writer).

opcodes.name: 16-bit reciprocal into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: Table-only `.a` reciprocal from a 16-bit source; seen only as a decode of a flipped MMA bit.

opcodes.name: hardware reciprocal
opcodes.what: 1/x in one instruction; within 1 ulp, correctly rounded on 931 of 1,024 probes.

opcodes.name: round to nearest even
opcodes.what: Metal `rint`: rounds fp32 to the nearest integer, ties to even.

opcodes.name: floor
opcodes.what: Rounds fp32 down to an integer (denormals to zero).

opcodes.name: fp32 truncate toward zero
opcodes.what: d = trunc(a); the sign of a zero result is kept (op3818.trunc, q3818).

opcodes.name: rsqrt seed
opcodes.what: Hardware 1/sqrt(x); an exact function tabulated in isa/g17-rsqrt-seed.npz, 1 ulp off on 50 of 1,024 probes; returns +inf at 0.

opcodes.name: trig-family op, function unmeasured
opcodes.what: Emitted by cos/sin/cospi; deliberately left without an invented function in 24.4.

opcodes.name: sqrt-safe rsqrt
opcodes.what: The rsqrt Apple uses for `fast_sqrt` (then a multiply): returns 1.0 at 0, where op3850 returns +inf, so x * rsqrt(x) is 0 rather than NaN.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, fp32 x fp32, accumulate
opcodes.what: 16x16x16 tensor-unit MMA with fp32 A and fp32 B into an fp32 accumulator; fp32 operands have their low 13 mantissa bits cleared, and it costs the same as half x half.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, fp32 x fp32, no accumulator
opcodes.what: The zero-C sibling of op5098: fp32 x fp32 16x16x16 MMA that ignores the accumulator.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, fp32 A x 16-bit B, accumulate
opcodes.what: 16x16x16 tensor-unit MMA with fp32 A and half-or-bfloat B into fp32; emitted under relaxed_precision for mixed float forms.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, fp32 A x 16-bit B, no accumulator
opcodes.what: The zero-C sibling of op5100.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, 16-bit A x fp32 B, accumulate
opcodes.what: 16x16x16 tensor-unit MMA with half-or-bfloat A and fp32 B into fp32.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, 16-bit A x fp32 B, no accumulator
opcodes.what: The zero-C sibling of op5104.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, 16-bit x 16-bit, accumulate
opcodes.what: The main 16x16x16 tensor-unit multiply-accumulate: half or bfloat A and B into an fp32 accumulator tuple; the workhorse of every prefill GEMM and attention kernel.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, 16-bit x 16-bit, no accumulator
opcodes.what: The zero-C sibling of op5106, starting a fresh accumulator; back-to-back issue into the same destination stalls about 34 ns (write-after-write).

opcodes.name: table-only narrow-accumulator MMA, first
opcodes.what: First of the 36 table-only declarations op5108-op5143 (16-bit accumulator forms with a four-word destination); no known CPU admits them and Apple emits none, so their subtypes are unrecovered.

opcodes.name: table-only narrow-accumulator MMA, last, no accumulator
opcodes.what: Last declaration of the op5108-op5143 table-only range, the no-accumulator variant; never emitted or admitted, subtype unrecovered.

opcodes.name: fp32 to 32-bit integer
opcodes.what: Converts fp32 to int/uint (both signednesses), register destination.

opcodes.name: half to 32-bit integer
opcodes.what: Converts a 16-bit half to a 32-bit integer, register destination.

opcodes.name: half to 16-bit integer
opcodes.what: Converts half to ushort/short, 16-bit register destination.

opcodes.name: fp32 to u32 into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` cvt: fp32 to 32-bit integer written to the uniform/staging file.

opcodes.name: half to 32-bit integer into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` cvt from half; operand 3 is 4 unsigned, 5 signed; truncates toward zero.

opcodes.name: half compare, chained into a flag
opcodes.what: flag = (half(x) REL 0.0) ? flag_in : 0; -0.0 compares as zero and NaN false.

opcodes.name: fp32 compare-select, fmax/fmin
opcodes.what: Four-register float select whose operation field gives fmax or fmin (Metal float max/min); used for clamps.

opcodes.name: 32-bit compare-select, immediate arms
opcodes.what: Compare-select on a 32-bit source with immediate results (the `csel` sibling); function only partly separated.

opcodes.name: float compare-select, fselect form
opcodes.what: Float compare-select from a 16-bit and a 32-bit source, cc 0 (==).

opcodes.name: float compare-select, csel form
opcodes.what: Float compare-select from a 16-bit and a 32-bit source, cc 0 (==); the csel-named sibling of op9748.

opcodes.name: half compare-select
opcodes.what: Four-register 16-bit float select (half clamp, min, max).

opcodes.name: half compare-select against minifloat
opcodes.what: d16 = (x16 cc K) ? a16 : b16 with a minifloat comparand K; source modifier 20 is abs(x).

opcodes.name: find most significant bit
opcodes.what: Index of the highest set bit (clz is derived from it).

opcodes.name: msb bit scan, 16-bit result
opcodes.what: Most-significant-bit scan (the op9986 form) with its destination narrowed to a 16-bit register.

opcodes.name: 64-bit no-return atomic, max/min
opcodes.what: no-return atomic that 64-bit atomic_max/atomic_min select; the map name says exchange.

opcodes.name: per-lane-address no-return atomic
opcodes.what: device atomic RMW at a per-lane address whose result is unused.

opcodes.name: uniform-address no-return atomic, 32-bit
opcodes.what: device 32-bit atomic RMW at a uniform address whose result is unused.

opcodes.name: uniform-address no-return compare-exchange
opcodes.what: no-return compare-and-exchange at a uniform address (operation code 262659); the register pair (expected, desired) is the '64' in its map name.

opcodes.name: per-lane-address atomic, returning
opcodes.what: device atomic RMW at a per-lane address; compiler-generated 12-byte ADD, AND, OR, SUB and XOR publishing on slot 7 updated and returned all 64 old values below Metal (two Submits per direct-store shape). ADD and XOR old+1 ALU consumers also passed. Authored floating ADD returned old +1.0f/-1.0f words while updating independent cells to 2.0f/+0.0f. A separate authored contention trial updated one word to 65.0f and returned all 64 old values 1.0f..64.0f exactly once in two pure Submits. An OR near miss executed exchange until byte11[4] was cleared; the same bit enables the 12-byte AND form to decode. Other consumed fetch operations remain refused by the compiler.
sections: 25.115.1; `docs/g17-first-dispatch-trials.md` compiler-generated integer and authored floating ADD return trials

opcodes.name: per-lane-address compare-exchange, returning
opcodes.what: device compare-and-exchange at a per-lane address; a hand-authored 12-byte form publishing on slot 7 returned all 64 old values in two pure below-Metal Submits, covering one successful and 63 failed compares. Compiler-generated 60-byte whole programs then passed ten more pure Submits over index registers R0, R1, R5, R7 and R12; the other R0..R12 placements decode-check but are not individually executed.
sections: 25.59; `docs/g17-first-dispatch-trials.md` authored and compiler-generated compare-exchange return trials

opcodes.name: uniform-address atomic, returning old
opcodes.what: device atomic RMW at a uniform address returning the old value; the return fills scoreboard slot 7.

opcodes.name: uniform-address compare-exchange, returning
opcodes.what: device compare-and-exchange at a uniform address whose result is used.

opcodes.name: 32-bit saturating add
opcodes.what: d = a + b clamped; signedness is a source modifier (16/32 unsigned, 24/40 signed).

opcodes.name: 64-bit add
opcodes.what: d64 = a64 + b64; forms buffer base + offset addresses.

opcodes.name: 32-bit add immediate
opcodes.what: d = a32 + imm (8-bit); the loop-carried pointer advance when it fits.

opcodes.name: 32-bit add
opcodes.what: d = a32 + b32, two registers.

opcodes.name: add, 32-bit plus zero-extended 16-bit
opcodes.what: d = a32 + low16(b), mod 2^32; with a = 0 it is cc's u16_to_u32 widening (t10283, g10283).

opcodes.name: add 16-bit to 32-bit
opcodes.what: d32 = zext16(a) + b32; executed on Apple's GPU, with a full-width a that separates zero- from sign-extension (25.195).

opcodes.name: 16-bit plus 16-bit, 32-bit result
opcodes.what: d32 = a16 + b16, widening.

opcodes.name: 16-bit add immediate
opcodes.what: d16 = a16 + imm, wrapping at 16 bits; executed on Apple's GPU over 4,096 lanes (25.195).

opcodes.name: 32-bit add immediate into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` add: a32 + imm to the uniform/staging file; a constant-program uniform writer.

opcodes.name: 32-bit add into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` add of two registers to the uniform/staging file.

opcodes.name: 32-bit compare with immediate into a flag
opcodes.what: flag = (a32 cc imm), the loop-exit compare (10-byte form; uint counter; int gives the 6-byte width).

opcodes.name: 16-bit compare into a flag
opcodes.what: flag = (a16 cc ...), the per-simdgroup bound compare.

opcodes.name: 16-bit register compare into a flag
opcodes.what: flag = (a16 cc b16); not a select despite the `csel` name.

opcodes.name: 32-bit compare with immediate into a flag, short form
opcodes.what: The 6-byte sibling of op10369; signed test against 0 in loop breaks.

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, int8 widening to int32
opcodes.what: 16x16x16 int8/uint8 MMA into int32 at twice the fp16 issue rate; wraps by default, and byte8 bit 4 selects a measured saturating variant (one signed clip of C + A.B).

opcodes.name: tensor MMA, int8 widening, no accumulator
opcodes.what: The zero-C sibling of op10384.

opcodes.name: 32 x immediate to 64-bit product
opcodes.what: d64 = a32 * imm; the map's `mulhi` is wrong.

opcodes.name: 64-bit address multiply-add
opcodes.what: d64 = a64 + b32 * imm; forms 64-bit addresses. The map's `mulhi` is wrong.

opcodes.name: 32 x 32 to 64-bit product
opcodes.what: d64 = a32 * b32 (the low word is the low product); shares the `mulhi` name with op10790.

opcodes.name: 32 x 32 + 32 to 64-bit multiply-add
opcodes.what: d64 = a*b + c, unsigned.

opcodes.name: multiply by immediate, 32-bit addend
opcodes.what: d = a32 * imm + b32.

opcodes.name: multiply by immediate, 16-bit addend
opcodes.what: d = a * imm + zext16(b); the map's `mul` omits the addend.

opcodes.name: 32-bit multiply
opcodes.what: d = a32 * b32, low 32 bits.

opcodes.name: 32-bit multiply-add
opcodes.what: d = a32 * b32 + c32, low 32 bits (the lanes receipt's fit, 32/32 lanes).

opcodes.name: multiply-add, 16-bit multiplier
opcodes.what: d = a32 * zext16(b) + c32.

opcodes.name: multiply-add, 16-bit multiplier and addend
opcodes.what: d = a32 * zext16(b) + zext16(c).

opcodes.name: 16-bit multiply by immediate plus immediate
opcodes.what: d32 = zext16(a) * imm + imm.

opcodes.name: multiply-add, 16-bit multiplicand
opcodes.what: d = zext16(a) * b32 + c32.

opcodes.name: multiply-add, 16-bit multiplicand and addend
opcodes.what: d = zext16(a) * b32 + zext16(c).

opcodes.name: signed-by-unsigned 16-bit multiply-add
opcodes.what: d = sext16(a) * zext16(b) + c32.

opcodes.name: 16-bit multiply by immediate plus immediate, 16-bit result
opcodes.what: d16 = a16 * imm + imm.

opcodes.name: multiply by immediate plus immediate into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` madd: a * imm + imm to the uniform/staging file.

opcodes.name: 32-bit multiply into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` multiply of two registers to the uniform/staging file; a constant-program writer.

opcodes.name: MMA bit-flip mutation artifact

opcodes.name: texture write

opcodes.name: 32-bit NOT into the uniform/staging file
opcodes.what: The `.a` NOT to the uniform/staging file.
